items.title: Using index-url only for a specific package
items.body:
### Question

Hello,

I want to use PyTorch with Docling, but I have an old GPU, so I need to use a specific version of CUDA for that. To install Torch with the right CUDA version, I use the command:

``uv add torch torchvision --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu126``

Then I use the command:

``uv pip install docling``

If I use ``uv add docling``, then `torch` and `torchvision` are reinstalled without the `index-url`, so the CUDA version does not match my GPU's CUDA version.

```
 - torch==2.10.0+cu126
 + torch==2.10.0
 - torchvision==0.25.0+cu126
 + torchvision==0.25.0
```

I could use `default-index` instead of `index-url`:

``(warning: Indexes specified via `--index-url` will not be persisted to the `pyproject.toml` file; use `--default-index` instead.)``

But if I do that, I can only install `torch` because no other packages are in the Torch registry.
Using pip install ... don't save the package in pyproject.toml and uv.lock.

So my question is, what is the right way to do this using `uv`? How can I specify a specific `index-url` for one package?

items.title: SHA mismatch if wheel has no sha in the index, but sdist has
items.body:
### Summary

We have an internal simple index API (html) at the company, and due to some issues some artifacts don't have `#sha256=...` suffix in the link. Specifically, some packages have sha in sdist link, but not in wheel link.
When UV creates a lockfile, it won't put sha for these wheels into the lockfile, and will write only sha for sdist, reflecting the state of the index.

If I check the lockfile, it looks like this:
```toml
[[package]]
name = "somepackage"
version = "1.0.19"
source = { registry = "https://internal-index" }
dependencies = ["...redacted..."]
sdist = { url = "https://internal-storage/somepackage-1.0.19.tar.gz", hash = "sha256:9e7a94344c6fb4f792eaa7c881693af0edc157e88c497e2606efd94ad7d0c686" }
wheels = [
    { url = "https://internal-storage/somepackage-1.0.19-py3-none-any.whl" },
]
```

However, when trying to `uv sync`, uv will fail like so:
```shell
(venv310) user@pc [ ~/repos/somerepo ]$ uv sync --active --locked --group test
Resolved 377 packages in 4ms
  × Failed to download `somepackage==1.0.19`
  ╰─▶ Hash mismatch for `somepackage==1.0.19`

      Expected:
        sha256:9e7a94344c6fb4f792eaa7c881693af0edc157e88c497e2606efd94ad7d0c686

      Computed:
        sha256:79b282a73f3d5717191011ffdb7d94d9cebb4942f82f288eba8ea66721ae5203
```

When I used `-v` for more debug, I saw that uv downloads the wheel.
Looks like uv tries to use SHA from sdist when verifying downloaded wheel file:
```shell
(venv310) user@pc [ ~/repos/somerepo ]$ curl -s https://internal-storage/somepackage-1.0.19-py3-none-any.whl | sha256sum
79b282a73f3d5717191011ffdb7d94d9cebb4942f82f288eba8ea66721ae5203  -
```

Sounds like a bug!

### Platform

Azure Linux 2

### Version

0.6.10

### Python version

3.10.14

items.title: Issues creating a cuda-enabled pytorch environment with UV
items.body:
I'm having some issues using `uv lock` & `uv sync` in a package that needs to use cuda-enabled pytorch wheels.

Here's a minimal-ish reproduction:

https://github.com/pstjohn/uv-torchvision-repro
The workspace stuff is there since I'd like to eventually get this working in a monorepo-like environment (#6935)

The desired behavior would be that `uv lock` would match what I get with 
`pip install --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu124 torch torchvision`, which would be (at the time of writing) to install torch 2.4.1 and torchvision 0.19.1 both in their linux_x86_64 / cu124 / cp310 variants.

But instead I get the following error: 
```
0.197 error: distribution torchvision==0.15.0 @ registry+https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu124 
can't be installed because it doesn't have a source distribution or wheel for the current platform
```

If I use `uv pip install --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu124 torch torchvision`, I get `torch==2.4.1+cu124` and `torchvision==0.2.0`. (i.e., seemingly not pulling torchvision from the cu124 index).

Any thoughts on where I might be going wrong? Thanks!

items.title: `uv add` leaks credentials to `tool.uv.index` when `UV_DEFAULT_INDEX` is set
items.body:
I have a project that uses a private JFrog Artifactory repository to host internal packages, and as a proxy for PyPi. I just noticed that calling `uv add internal_package==specific_version` when overriding with `UV_DEFAULT_INDEX` will leak credentials into the `pyproject.toml` file, even if the lockfile isn't modified.

Original index entry (company name redacted):
```
# Set JFrog Artifactory as the default index.
[[tool.uv.index]]
name = "internal"
url = "https://repos.internal.com/artifactory/api/pypi/internal-pypi/simple"
default = true
```
Command (a no-op, since the package version already exists as a dependency):
```
$uv add internal_package==version
Resolved M packages in 2ms
Audited N packages in 0.87ms
```

After running that command, the `tool.uv.index` section has removed the `name = internal` line, inserted the full repo URL, including authentication tokens, and removed the comments:
```
[[tool.uv.index]]
url = "https://USERNAME:REDACTED@repos.internal.com/artifactory/api/pypi/internal-pypi/simple"
default = true
```

Summary:
* I was not expecting credentials to get saved to `pyproject.toml`
* I was not expecting that setting `UV_DEFAULT_INDEX` before running `uv add` would modify `pyproject.toml` at all (including removing comments).

uv version 0.4.25
